title: Access Control Policy Generation for IoT Using Deep Generative Models
summary: This conference paper proposes generating access control policy data for IoT systems using deep generative models, evaluated via a case study on the CAV policies dataset from Cunnington et al. The authors train CTGAN and CopulaGAN both with and without environmental constraints, then assess results using synthesis (quality) scores, visual correlation comparisons, and TSTR-style ML efficacy F1 tests across multiple classifiers. SDV's CTGAN and CopulaGAN are run as the two baseline generative models producing all the synthetic access-control policy data the empirical study rests on.
evidence: "We conducted a case study using two baseline Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) models, namely CTGAN and CopulaGAN, to generate access control policy data."
venue: 2025 IEEE 22nd Consumer Communications & Networking Conference (CCNC)

title: Adapted GAN-Based Models Efficiently Generate Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Longitudinal Clinical Biomarker Data
summary: This paper benchmarks GAN-based tabular synthesizers (CTGAN, CopulaGAN) adapted for multi-sequence data against the sequential model CPAR to generate privacy-preserving synthetic longitudinal prostate-cancer biomarker records, evaluating fidelity, predictive utility, privacy risk, and computational efficiency on a dataset of nearly 20,000 patients. The entire empirical programme runs SDV-ecosystem synthesizers directly: CTGAN and CopulaGAN (with their mode-specific normalization and Gaussian-copula components, via RDT for transforms) and CPAR/Sequential SDV as evaluation subjects, with fidelity and disclosure metrics computed via SDMetrics' Column Shape/Pair Trend scores and Disclosure Protection Estimate. SDV's CTGAN, CopulaGAN, and CPAR synthesizers are run as the generators under comparison, forming the entire empirical results of the paper.

Within the Sequential SDV framework [4], which includes CPAR, a post-processing step is applied to transform the generated sequential outputs back into a tabular format."
venue: IEEE Access

summary: This paper proposes an Adaptive Block-LSTM model, tuned by a genetic algorithm, to predict arcing-induced temperatures in subway pantograph-catenary systems from scarce and imbalanced operational data. To overcome the unavailability and sparsity of real metro data, the authors use kernel density estimation to guide block partitioning and train a CTGAN, initialized with a metadata object and with enforce_min_max_values=True, on the full dataset to generate a privacy-preserving synthetic dataset that underpins all subsequent modeling. CTGAN (via what appears to be the SDV-family synthesizer API, given the enforce_min_max_values parameter) is the sole generator producing the training data for the whole empirical pipeline.

title: Adaptive CTGAN: Data Augmentation for Imbalanced Cybersecurity Datasets
summary: This paper proposes Adaptive CTGAN (A-CTGAN), a modification of the CTGAN architecture for tabular data augmentation that adds a learnable class-embedding layer and a dynamic, loss-weighted conditional sampling mechanism to better handle severe class imbalance. Evaluated on the CIC-IDS-2017 network intrusion detection benchmark using a Train-on-Synthetic, Test-on-Real protocol, A-CTGAN is compared against SMOTE, a vanilla GAN, a conditional GAN, and standard CTGAN, showing improved minority-class F1 and lower KL divergence. The standard CTGAN baseline is implemented via the CTGANSynthesizer class from the sdv library, and Adaptive CTGAN is built by subclassing this SDV synthesizer and overriding its fit method and data sampler.

title: Anonymization of Private and Confidential Ground Data for Earth Observation Data Analytics such as Socioeconomic Data
summary: This IGARSS conference paper proposes a pragmatic definition of data anonymization for ground-truth socioeconomic survey data used to label Earth Observation imagery, combining differential-privacy noise with synthetic data generation to preserve statistical fidelity while removing identifiable values. The authors test a Laplacian-noise approach against fully synthetic data, showing the synthetic route better preserves the original distribution without incorporating real values, then train ML models on the anonymized data to assess information-leakage risk. CTGAN is run directly to generate the anonymized synthetic dataset that forms the core of the empirical demonstration.
evidence: "Instead of adding noise to the original dataset, we can create an entirely synthetic dataset using CTGAN [14]... In Figure 3, the CTGAN synthetic data reproduce the statistical distribution of the original dataset whereas none of the original values are actually incorporated in the dataset."
venue: IGARSS 2024 - 2024 IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium

title: De-anonymizing VR Avatars using Non-VR Motion Side-channels
summary: This paper demonstrates a novel privacy attack that de-anonymizes VR users by correlating their avatar's visual movements with motion-sensor data from a separate non-VR wearable device, using an activity-classification and identity-ranking pipeline. To evaluate the attack at large scale, the authors generate a synthetic dataset of one million activity sequences. CTGAN is trained on real participants' activity sequences and run to generate this large-scale synthetic dataset used in the evaluation.

title: Application of a Data Augmentation Technique on Blast-Induced Fly-Rock Distance Prediction
summary: This book chapter addresses data scarcity in blast-induced fly-rock distance prediction by augmenting a small dataset (131 samples) of measurements from four Malaysian granite quarries using a tabular variational autoencoder, then validating the synthetic data statistically and using it to train five machine learning prediction models. Results show that mixing true and synthetic training data outperforms using either alone. The TVAE model used to generate the synthetic data is explicitly identified as being provided by the open-source SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) library, which is run directly as the generator underpinning the entire empirical study.

The authors expand small-class samples using CTGAN and tune hyperparameters following recommendations of the CTGAN library, evaluating the impact of synthetic sample size on downstream prediction accuracy. summary: This paper proposes the Mutual Information Autoencoder (MIAE), an ex ante privacy-preserving model that treats privacy-attribute information leaked through public attributes as noise, combining reconstruction error and mutual information in its loss to achieve utility-privacy trade-offs grounded in rate-distortion theory. title: Generating Synthetic Data is Complicated: Know Your Data and Know Your Generator

CTGAN, explicitly identified as part of the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) package, is run as one of three generators evaluated, with its hyperparameters tuned and its GAN-based approach discussed as a source of utility limitations.

Experiments on three imbalanced tabular datasets compare classifiers trained on real, sampled-balanced, and GAN-synthesized data. CTGAN is used with its default settings as the baseline tabular GAN against which I2TGANF's image-GAN-based synthetic data is compared for downstream ML classifier performance.

CTGAN is run as one of two candidate generators evaluated in this comparative pipeline, using its conditional generator/discriminator design to model the tabular attack data.

summary: This paper presents GenEthos, an interactive GUI tool for synthetic tabular data generation that incorporates bias detection (via metrics like SPD and DI) and bias mitigation algorithms (e.g., Learning Fair Representation) for datasets such as German Credit and Adult. title: Predicting IoT Distributed Ledger Fraud Transactions With a Lightweight GAN Network
summary: This paper proposes VecGAN, a lightweight GAN-based data augmentation method for predicting fraudulent transactions in resource-constrained IoT distributed ledger (blockchain) networks, aiming to replace computationally intensive Proof-of-Work consensus with machine-learning classification. VecGAN combines error-driven learning with Bayesian estimation and a dual-purpose discriminator to handle rare double-spend fraud events under class imbalance, improving classifier accuracy over other augmentation baselines while reducing computation. CTGAN was tested as a comparison baseline but was rejected after performing poorly on large datasets with long training times and high computation.
affiliations: Missouri University of Science and Technology
Missouri University of Science and Technology
evidence: "Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) [29] was also considered, but performed poorly on large datasets in separate experiments with long training times and high computation."
venue: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

title: Predicting Music Sentiment: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models Before and After Feature Selection
summary: This conference paper compares five machine learning classifiers (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Decision Tree, SVM, K-Nearest Neighbours) for sentiment analysis of music lyrics, evaluating accuracy before and after feature selection. To address a skewed-class problem in their dataset, the authors state they use the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) package to generate augmented data. The SDV paper on sequential models (PAR) is cited only in a general explanatory sentence about synthetic data's applications, not tied to a specific algorithm run.
evidence: "Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) which is a groundbreaking package that offers impressive features for generating datasets will be used [12]... Its applications range from protecting the privacy of real data to creating enhanced, augmented datasets for data science [13]."
venue: 28th International Conference on Information Technology (IT)
needs: The sequential-2022 (PAR) citation [13] supports a generic statement about synthetic data's uses; the actual SDV package usage claim is attached to a different, non-SDV-family reference [12], so whether SDV code was actually run for this specific cited paper is unclear.

title: Predicting Postgraduate Student Engagement Using Artificial Intelligence (AI)
summary: This paper develops AI/ML classification models to predict multiple dimensions of postgraduate international-student engagement from a small (96-response) survey, using synthetic data generation to augment the limited dataset before training classifiers such as random forest and extra trees. The authors generate and compare synthetic data from GaussianCopula, TVAE, CopulaGAN, and CTGAN, selecting the best-performing method per engagement dimension via KSTest scores, with CTGAN and GaussianCopula outputs driving most of the reported predictions. CTGAN, run alongside SDV's other tabular synthesizers (GaussianCopula, CopulaGAN, TVAE), is used to generate the synthetic training data underlying the study's headline accuracy results.
evidence: "We tried the four methods of GaussianCopula, TVAE, CopulaGAN, and CTGAN (as discussed above) and since the accuracies for CTGAN were higher, we proceeded with all the simulations with CTGAN (100 synthetic data + 96 original data)."
needs: Affiliations not printed in the extracted first-page text; venue name not given in evidence though DOI suggests IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence.

title: Prediction of Cardiovascular Disease Risk and Risk Factor Assessment in Diabetic Patients Based on Deep Learning and Interpretability Methods
summary: This conference paper builds a TabNet-based deep learning model to predict cardiovascular disease risk in diabetic patients using NHANES survey data, addressing class imbalance in the dataset with a GAN-based approach, and uses SHAP to identify key risk factors such as waist circumference, age, and BMI. The paper states it 'employs Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) methods to address the prominent issue of sample imbalance,' citing the CTGAN paper as reference [10], but the extracted full text gives no further detail on how CTGAN was implemented or applied. CTGAN is cited as the GAN methodology referenced for oversampling minority (high-risk) cases, without visible evidence it was run via the SDV library itself.
evidence: "This study employs Generative Adversarial Network(GAN) methods to address the prominent issue of sample imbalance caused by the scarcity of positive samples in the medical field," with reference [10] cited as Xu L, Skoularidou M, Cuesta-Infante A, Veeramachaneni K.(2019) Modeling Tabular data using Conditional GAN.
needs: Full text gives no description of how CTGAN was implemented (own reimplementation vs SDV library) or applied to the imbalance problem; cannot confirm api_user vs port vs citation_only with certainty.

title: Prediction of displacement of composite slab with profiled steel deck using artificial neural network
summary: This paper trains feedforward artificial neural networks, optimised with Bayesian regularisation, to predict the maximum displacement of composite slabs with profiled steel decking, using a combined dataset of prior experimental results and additional synthetic samples. Because available experimental data were limited, the authors used the Python TGAN module to generate synthetic tabular training data that was merged with real datasets before training the ANN models. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni, 2018) is run directly via its Python package as the generator producing the synthetic augmentation data underlying part of the training set.
affiliations: SRM Institute of Science and Technology
SRM Institute of Science and Technology
evidence: "TGAN was implemented in this study using the Python TGAN module after tabular dataset analysis with both types of variables confirmed its usefulness. The TGAN parameters of current study are detailed in Table 2."
venue: Asian Journal of Civil Engineering

title: Prediction of forming accuracy and process parameter optimization for SPS-SPIF
summary: This manufacturing engineering paper proposes a hybrid CTGAN-DBN-NSGA-II framework for predicting axial and radial forming accuracy in Static Pressure Support-Single Point Incremental Forming (SPS-SPIF), using CTGAN to augment a small experimental dataset, a Deep Belief Network to model the parameter-accuracy relationship, and NSGA-II for multi-objective process optimization. The generated data's fidelity is validated using KL divergence and SDMetrics' coverage quality evaluation against SMOTE and VAE baselines. CTGAN is run as the core data-augmentation generator underpinning the entire empirical pipeline, and SDMetrics is used directly to evaluate the synthetic data's distributional quality.
affiliations: Xi'an Huanyu Satellite Control and Data Application Co., Ltd
evidence: "SDMetrics quality evaluation: SDMetrics is a toolkit designed to assess the quality of generated data... coverage quality evaluation provided by SDMetrics was used to assess the probability distribution of the data generated by CTGAN." CTGAN augmentation underlies the entire CTGAN-DBN-NSGA-II modeling pipeline.
venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
needs: CTGAN itself is cited (mis-attributed to 'Lei et al.') rather than named as a package import; hyperparameter table names differ slightly from standard sdv-dev CTGAN constructor args, but explicit use of SDMetrics as a named toolkit supports api_user integration.

title: Prediction Model for Academic Burnout Using Machine Learning in University Students
summary: This paper proposes an XGBoost-based predictive model to identify Peruvian university students at risk of academic burnout, using survey data on 18 academic, emotional and contextual variables with the OLBI-S instrument as target. To overcome the small original sample of 71 students, the authors augment the dataset to 300 instances and validate feature-level fidelity via the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test before deploying the model as a FastAPI service. CTGAN from the SDV library is run directly as the data augmentation engine that expands the training set on which the whole predictive pipeline rests.
evidence: "synthetic data were generated using the CTGAN model from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, expanding the sample to 300 instances"
venue: ICAT 2025 (CCIS 2949)

title: Preserving Privacy in Marketing: A Comparative Study of Synthetic Data for Personalized Campaign Generation
summary: This conference paper builds a GAN-based synthetic customer data generator paired with an LLM-driven campaign generation pipeline, comparing marketing campaigns produced from synthetic versus real customer records via automated LLM scoring and a 200-participant human survey. The authors implement two GAN variants for the generator: a standard GAN and their own CTGAN-style architecture that conditions on categorical columns to handle multimodal and imbalanced categorical features. This CTGAN variant is a from-scratch reimplementation of the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN design, not the sdv-dev library, used as one of the two generators evaluated in the empirical comparison.
evidence: "The second is a CTGAN, a specialized variant designed to condition on categorical columns in order to better capture multimodal distributions and handle imbalanced categories."
venue: 2025 3rd International Conference on Recent Advances in Information Technology for Sustainable Development (ICRAIS)
needs: The reference list cites Patki et al. 2016 (SDV) as [18], but no body-text passage engaging with SDV itself was found; the substantive engagement is with a self-built CTGAN-style architecture rather than the sdv-dev package.

title: From Principle to Practice: Vertical Data Minimization for Machine Learning
summary: This paper proposes vertical data minimization (vDM), a workflow based on data generalization that ensures no full-resolution client data is collected during ML training or deployment, and introduces Privacy-aware Tree (PAT), an algorithm that outperforms baseline vDM methods across several settings. The paper contrasts its generalization-based approach against the synthetic data setting as an alternative privacy-preserving paradigm. TGAN and CTGAN are cited only as examples of the synthetic data generation literature the authors position their work against, with no evidence either was run.
evidence: Unlike the synthetic data setting [51], [64], in vDM, each x ∼ D_orig is directly mapped to exactly one z = g(x); [64] is CTGAN and [46]/[47] TGAN-related, cited only in the reference list, never run in experiments.
venue: 2024 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
needs: The whole text was searched and confirms no SDV-family term appears outside the reference list/contrastive citation, so this is bibliographic only.

title: Prism: Private Relational Data Synthesis with Language Models
summary: This paper presents Prism, an end-to-end framework for differentially private (DP) relational data synthesis that distills knowledge from an ensemble of teacher LLMs into a student generator via DP output aggregation, using token pruning, adaptive noise scaling, and threshold-filtered probabilistic sampling to improve the privacy-utility trade-off. It is evaluated against eight state-of-the-art baselines across twelve experiments on tabular datasets like Adult. CTGAN is cited as the base architecture underlying two DP baseline methods, DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN, which are run as comparison baselines but not CTGAN itself.
evidence: "3 PATE-CTGAN [43, 85] and 4 DP-CTGAN [84] are CTGAN [96]-based synthesizers that achieve DP by PATE and DP-SGD, respectively." -- CTGAN is cited as the underlying model for two baseline methods but is not itself run.
venue: Proc. ACM Manag. Data (SIGMOD)
needs: Unclear whether DP-CTGAN/PATE-CTGAN baselines were run via the SDV-dev CTGAN package or independent reimplementations; treated as citation_only per descendant rule since no SDV library invocation is evidenced.

title: Privacy Analysis of Oblivious DNS over HTTPS: a Website Fingerprinting Study
summary: This paper investigates the resilience of Oblivious DNS-over-HTTPS (ODoH) against website fingerprinting attacks using a GENI testbed and deep learning classifiers, showing a passive adversary can identify visited websites with 94% accuracy, and it prototypes a mitigation strategy. As part of that mitigation, the authors use the Synthetic Data Vault to capture the joint distribution of traffic features (packet sizes, timing) from real traces and generate synthetic samples that blend with real traffic to simulate a worst-case attacker scenario. SDV is run as a generator producing synthetic traffic traces used to bolster the proposed defense mechanism.
evidence: "To achieve this, Synthetic Data Vault captures the joint distribution of these features from real traces and generates new samples that preserve the same statistical properties, ensuring the synthetic traces blend seamlessly with actual traffic."
venue: 2025 55th Annual IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Dependable Systems and Networks (DSN)
needs: The specific SDV synthesizer (e.g., GaussianCopula) is not named explicitly, only inferred from the 'joint distribution' description characteristic of SDV's core method.

title: Privacy Assessment of Synthetic Patient Data
summary: This paper quantifies the privacy gain of synthetic patient data generated by two differentially private generative models, MST and PrivBayes, trained on real anonymized UK primary-care patient data from CPRD Aurum. Using the TAPAS toolbox, the authors evaluate membership and attribute inference attacks under black-box threat models, finding PrivBayes more robust than MST though both remain vulnerable for some outlier records. CTGAN is only mentioned in a list of generators found in the literature and is not used to generate or evaluate any of the paper's synthetic data.
affiliations: Brunel University London; Medicine and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
Medicine and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
evidence: "Several generators have been introduced in the literature to produce synthetic data such as MST [5], PrivBayes [6], CTGAN [16], PATEGAN [17], and SynthPop [18]. We used MST [5], and PrivBayes [6] for generating the synthetic data."
venue: 2023 IEEE 36th International Symposium on Computer-Based Medical Systems (CBMS)

title: Privacy-Aware Health Digital Twins Using Centralized Differential Privacy and Tabular VAE
summary: This paper proposes CDP-TVAE, a framework that applies centralized differential privacy noise through a data-trust middleware before training a Tabular Variational Autoencoder to generate privacy-preserving synthetic health digital twins from wearable sleep and activity data. It benchmarks CDP-TVAE and CDP-Gaussian Copula against PATE-CTGAN and DP-CTGAN baselines, evaluating fidelity, ML utility, and membership-inference privacy risk. TVAE, GaussianCopula and CTGAN are run directly as the SDV library's synthesizers, and SDMetrics is used to compute quality scores and ML efficacy metrics throughout the empirical evaluation.
evidence: "In this study, we focus on applying our proposed central differential privacy (CDP) approach to TVAE and Gaussian Copula models from the SDV library... The smartnoise-synth Python library was utilized to perform the experiments of PATE-CTGAN and DP-CTGAN." Also: "we used the Linear Regression (LR) model from the SDMetrics to compute the R2 score" (footnote: https://docs.sdv.dev/sdmetrics/).
venue: 2026 IEEE World AI IoT Congress (AIIoT)

title: Privacy-Enhanced Point-of-Interest Recommendations Using Synthetic Data: A Comparative Study of CTGAN and Clustering Techniques
summary: This paper studies privacy-preserving point-of-interest recommender systems by training recommendation models solely on synthetic user data, comparing CTGAN-generated synthetic ratings against clustering-generated centroids and real data. It evaluates recommendation accuracy (via RMSE) when real users are entirely replaced by synthetic ones, showing synthetic data can preserve accuracy while protecting privacy. The authors explicitly adopt the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) framework's CTGAN implementation to generate the synthetic tabular user-rating data that underlies the entire experimental evaluation.
evidence: "We adopted a framework from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) for its compatibility with tabular data [21]." CTGAN is used to train recommender models entirely on synthetic data, compared against clustering-based synthesis and real data.
venue: 2025 IEEE 22nd Consumer Communications & Networking Conference (CCNC)

title: Privacy-preserving Approximate Query Processing with Differentially Private Generative Models
summary: This conference paper integrates several differentially private generative models (PATE-CTGAN, DP-CTGAN, DP-GAN) with an approximate query processing (AQP) engine, evaluating synthetic data quality and query relative error on a Parkinson's disease dataset. Non-private CTGAN is trained and used as a baseline against which the DP variants are compared, and the authors' quality assessment relies on the SDMetrics Quality Report tool to score column shapes and pair trends. CTGAN thus serves as the non-private comparison baseline while SDMetrics is run directly as the evaluation library underpinning the paper's quality metrics.
affiliations: Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute (ETRI); Sungshin Women's University
evidence: "CTGAN [10] is the baseline model for comparing the performance of other privacy-preserving generative models" and quality was assessed "using the SDMetrics Quality Report... an open-source Python library" (https://github.com/sdv-dev/SDMetrics).
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
needs: Unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev ctgan package directly or a separate implementation; SDMetrics use is explicit and directly linked to the sdv-dev GitHub repo.

title: Privacy-Preserving Blockchain Transactions Synthesis with Diffusion Generative Models
summary: This paper proposes BTGM, a diffusion-based generative model for synthesizing blockchain transaction data that combines differential privacy with a two-stage diffusion process and VGM-based Row Modeling, aiming to balance detection accuracy with privacy protection. Validated on the Elliptic++ dataset, BTGM is shown to outperform CTGAN and STaSy on utility metrics and downstream classification while better resisting membership inference attacks. CTGAN's GAN-based architecture and its mode-specific normalization are described as prior art and run as a baseline generator, with its synthetic output and downstream performance compared directly against BTGM's.
evidence: "generated by BTGM can achieve better usability results ... and can avoid the crash problem ... encountered by CTGAN and STaSy in downstream classification tasks"; Table I reports CTGAN's utility/task-specific metrics alongside PATE-GAN and BTGM.
venue: IIKI 2024 (International Conference on Intelligence and Knowledge Innovation)

title: Privacy-Preserving Generation of Synthetic Pathology Reports for Information Extraction
summary: This paper proposes a two-stage pipeline for generating synthetic clinical report/data pairs to support information extraction for breast cancer pathology reports in French: first synthesizing tabular variable-value data with a privacy-preserving synthesizer, then using LLMs to convert the tabular data into pathology-report text. It compares four tabular synthesizers from two libraries (SDV and SmartNoise) on fidelity, similarity and novelty, ultimately selecting PATE-CTGAN (from SmartNoise) for the final pipeline because it best balances fidelity and privacy. SDV's GaussianCopula and CTGAN synthesizers are run as two of the four evaluated baselines and are described in detail (including CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional sampling) but are not the model finally chosen for data generation.
evidence: "We compare four existing synthesizers from two libraries, Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) [11] and SmartNoise [8]: a probabilistic model based on copulas (Gaussian Copula from SDV), a generative adversarial network adapted to tabular data (CTGAN from SDV)... we therefore select PATE-CTGAN for synthetic medical data generation."
venue: AIME 2026

title: Privacy-Preserving Medical Data Generation Using Adversarial Learning
summary: This paper proposes RDP-VAEGAN, a framework combining Rényi Differential Privacy with a GAN and Variational Autoencoder to generate privacy-preserving synthetic medical data, evaluated against other privacy-constrained models on two public medical datasets. In the related-work section, CTGAN is mentioned as an approach specifically designed to handle tabular data with mixed continuous and discrete features, but it is only cited, not run or compared against experimentally. CTGAN is cited only in passing as prior related work.

Fraunhofer Institute for Toxicology and Experimental Medicine
Fraunhofer Institute for Toxicology and Experimental Medicine; Goethe University Frankfurt
evidence: "CTGAN [32] is specifically designed to handle tabular data comprising both continuous and discrete features" -- mentioned only in related work, not used in experiments.

title: Towards Privacy-Preserving Relational Data Synthesis via Probabilistic Relational Models
summary: This paper proposes a pipeline for generating synthetic multi-table relational data using probabilistic relational models, specifically parametric factor graphs, including a learning algorithm to construct such a model from a relational database. It positions this approach against existing single-table synthetic data generation methods based on GANs or Bayesian networks. CTGAN is cited only in the related-work discussion of GAN-based approaches, with no code run or comparison performed.
affiliations: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI)
evidence: 'While many popular approaches are based on generative adversarial networks [34/33 CTGAN], there are also approaches building on probabilistic graphical models such as Bayesian networks [13].' CTGAN appears only in this related-work sentence and the bibliography; no experiments involve it.
venue: KI 2024 (Springer LNAI 14992)

title: Privacy-Preserving Tabular Data Generation Based on Diffusion Models
summary: This paper proposes a hybrid diffusion model for generating privacy-preserving tabular data, combining differential privacy mechanisms with Gaussian diffusion for numerical attributes and multinomial diffusion for categorical attributes. It evaluates the approach on six public datasets against data utility and privacy metrics, comparing against existing tabular synthesis baselines and the state-of-the-art TabDDPM diffusion model. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline generators in the empirical comparison, with results reported in a data-utility table alongside the authors' own diffusion-based method.
evidence: "Our method was compared with CTGAN [21], TVAE [22], and CTABGAN+ [23], and showed good superiority," with CTGAN results reported in Table II's data utility comparison alongside the authors' proposed diffusion model.
venue: IEEE International Conference on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics (SMC)
needs: The paper's 'TVAE' baseline is cited to Ishfaq et al.'s unrelated triplet-based VAE paper, not SDV's TVAE, so that baseline was excluded from sdv_concept; only the CTGAN citation matches the SDV family per the provided evidence.

title: Privacy-Protected Person Re-Identification via Virtual Samples
summary: This paper addresses privacy leakage in person re-identification by proposing a Translation-Rendering-Sampling framework that generates virtual pedestrian images using privacy-irrelevant scene attributes (background, pose, illumination) instead of real captured appearances, trained on virtual samples like PersonX. The learned model is transferred to real target re-ID datasets without ever exposing person appearance during training. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of GAN-based methods prone to mode collapse, with no experimental use.
evidence: CTGAN is listed among 'GAN-based methods [43], [44], which are prone to modal [collapse]' in a citation list, with no experimental engagement.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

title: A Privacy Protected Sleep Quality Prediction Approach Using Ultrawideband Ambient Sensor, Synthetic Data, and Deep Learning
summary: This paper presents a sleep-quality assessment pipeline using an ultrawideband ambient radar sensor to record nighttime respiration, augmenting a small real dataset with synthetic data, categorizing samples with K-Nearest Neighbors, and modeling respiration-to-sleep-quality relationships with bidirectional LSTM networks. The work addresses data scarcity and privacy concerns by avoiding cloud-based wearables in favor of a privacy-preserving ambient sensor plus synthetic augmentation. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) is run directly as the tool that generates the synthetic respiration data used to augment training throughout the empirical evaluation.
evidence: "This work used the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) to generate synthetic data. Fig. 4 shows the frequency distribution of real and synthetic data using SDV."
venue: 2024 9th International Conference on Machine Learning Technologies (ICMLT)

title: Private Synthetic Data Generation for Mixed Type Datasets
summary: This paper proposes a hybrid private synthetic data generation pipeline for mixed-type datasets that combine structured and unstructured (text) columns, evaluated on Yelp reviews and drug side-effects data using a context-aware exposure metric alongside quality and privacy measures. In describing the structured-data component of their pipeline, the authors note that any GAN-based tabular synthesizer could be plugged in, citing CTGAN as one such option alongside TableGAN and UniformGAN. CTGAN is discussed as a candidate module for the structured-data stage rather than confirmed as the model actually run in their reported experiments.
evidence: "For the structured data generation, any GAN based structured data generation modules such as TableGAN [29], UniformGAN [4], or CTGAN [5] could be used provided they are capable of generating quality data that captures the distribution and characteristics of the original dataset..."
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (Big Data)
needs: Unclear whether CTGAN was actually implemented/run in the system's reported experiments or only mentioned as a pluggable design option; no results section referencing CTGAN specifically was found in the provided evidence.

title: PrivFly: A Privacy-Preserving Self-Supervised Framework for Rare Attack Detection in IoFT
summary: Proposes PrivFly, a privacy-preserving intrusion detection framework for the Internet of Flying Things that combines self-supervised masked-feature reconstruction with differential privacy, and uses SHAP analysis to study the privacy-utility tradeoff on the ECU-IoFT dataset. To address severe class imbalance, the authors augment rare attack classes using either CTGAN or SMOTE, comparing the resulting detection performance under varying differential-privacy noise levels. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of two data augmentation methods for oversampling minority attack classes.
evidence: "we performed a rare attack augmentation step using CTGAN or SMOTE methods, increasing the minority attack class from 10 to 500 total instances" with results reported as 'PrivFly + CTGAN' in comparison tables.
venue: IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC)
needs: Unclear whether the authors used the sdv-dev/ctgan package directly or their own reimplementation; no constructor parameters or import statements are shown.

title: Probabilistic Causal Modelling of Factors Contributing to Stress, Anxiety, and Depression for Nurses and Social Workers
summary: This paper analyzes survey and daily-diary data from nurses and social workers to uncover causal relationships among stress, anxiety, depression, and demographic/professional factors, combining reliability and correlation analysis with synthetic data generation and causal structure learning to compensate for a small sample size. To address data scarcity, the authors generate synthetic datasets using Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and TVAE models trained across multiple epochs, then run causal discovery algorithms on the resulting synthetic data, citing the SDV dissertation as the source of these techniques. SDV's Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and TVAE synthesizers are run directly as the data-generation stage whose output feeds the entire downstream causal-modelling experiment.
affiliations: University of Calgary; Mount Royal University
evidence: "We employed several synthetic data generation techniques [27]: Gaussian Copula ... CTGAN (Conditional Tabular GAN) ... TVAE (Tabular Variational Autoencoder) ... Each method was trained using multiple epochs (100, 300, 400, and 500)" citing the SDV dissertation as reference [27].

title: ProGen: Projection-Based Adversarial Attack Generation Against Network Intrusion Detection
summary: This paper proposes ProGen, a projection-based framework for generating adversarial network traffic against ML-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems, using a basic feature sequence representation and a traffic-space GAN with realistic constraints to evade detection while preserving traffic function. It is evaluated on CSE-CIC-IDS2018, CIC-IDS-2017, and UNSW-NB15 across six ML models. CTGAN is cited only in passing, attributed to a related work (PacketCGAN) that uses conditional GAN to address class imbalance, and is not run or engaged with directly by the authors.
evidence: "PacketCGAN [32] uses Conditional GAN [34] to generate traffic samples to solve the class imbalance issue." -- CTGAN paper [34] is cited only to describe another work's approach, not used or engaged with by ProGen itself.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

title: Protecting Multiple Sensitive Attributes in Synthetic Micro-data
summary: This paper extends a Bayesian-network-based synthetic data generation approach (built on DataSynthesizer) to protect multiple sensitive attributes from inference attacks while preserving data utility, evaluating two extension techniques on micro-data. The proposed methods are entirely based on Bayesian Networks, not on SDV; the Synthetic Data Vault (Gaussian copula based) is only cited as one of several existing synthetic data generation approaches and noted as a possible future direction for extending the sensitive-attribute protection technique, without being run.
evidence: In future, we will investigate how protecting sensitive attributes from disclosure can be performed in other data synthetisation methods, such as the synthetic data vault, which is based on Gaussian Copulas, or methods based on neural networks.
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)

title: Prototype of a Predictive System for Selecting Therapeutic Pets in Patients with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder
summary: This conference paper describes PetMatcher, an AI-based application that matches adolescent ADHD patients with therapeutic animals using clinical, emotional, and preference variables, and reports a predictive model trained and validated on a synthetic dataset of 200 simulated cases. The work focuses on animal-assisted therapy design rather than synthetic-data methodology itself. It cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper only to justify the general usefulness of simulated data in clinical research where real data access is restricted, without describing any SDV software being run.
evidence: Cites Patki, Wedge & Veeramachaneni's 'The Synthetic Data Vault' [27] solely to support: 'This type of simulated data is useful in exploratory research, especially when working with clinical populations where access to real data may be restricted for ethical or logistical reasons.'
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advances in Technology and Innovation (C366505 conference proceedings)
needs: No evidence any SDV software was actually run to generate the paper's own 200-case synthetic dataset; the citation appears purely rhetorical.

title: QaaD (Query-as-a-Data): Scalable Execution of Massive Number of Small Queries in Spark
summary: This paper presents QaaD, a technique for Apache Spark that transparently converts workloads of many small queries into larger merged queries and dynamically adjusts partition sizes, achieving 10.6x to 36.6x speedups over standard Spark for small-query workloads. To evaluate scalability across dataset sizes, the authors needed larger data volumes than their real marketplace datasets provided. SDV's Gaussian copula-based model is run as an API tool to generate synthetic records that expand the benchmark datasets to larger target sizes while preserving schema and statistical properties.
evidence: "We used SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) [22] tool to expand the dataset sizes... Specifically, we have used the Gaussian copula-based model provided by SDV to learn the data distribution."

title: A Quality Prediction Approach for Compressor Blade Manufacturing With Various Geometric Dimensions
summary: This paper proposes a domain generalization-based quality prediction framework for high-precision compressor blade manufacturing, using coordinate measuring machine (CMM) data from historical blades to predict geometric errors on newly designed blades without retraining. The framework is validated on four series of aerospace compressor blades from an industrial manufacturer, achieving low prediction errors across all four blade types. CTGAN (via the SDV-family CTGAN paper) is cited only in a passing reference to deep learning methods needing to meet generalization challenges, with no further engagement in the text.

title: Query Transformation for Approximate Query Processing Using Synthetic Data from Deep Generative Models
summary: This conference paper proposes query transformation rules for approximate query processing (AQP) engines that use synthetic data from arbitrary machine learning models, aiming to avoid dependence on any specific generative model. The authors run preliminary experiments generating synthetic versions of an Instacart grocery dataset and comparing AQP accuracy and execution time when the underlying synthetic data comes from different generators. CTGAN and TVAE, run via the open-source sdv-dev/CTGAN implementation, are the two synthesizers used to produce the synthetic data underlying the AQP evaluation.

title: RAC-GAN: Iterative Dual-Objective Over and Under Sampling for Imbalanced Datasets
summary: This paper proposes RAC-GAN, an end-to-end trainable framework that combines a GAN-based generator for oversampling with a reinforcement-learning ranker for undersampling, jointly optimizing both operations to improve classifier performance on imbalanced tabular datasets. It is evaluated on 11 real-world imbalanced datasets against heuristic and state-of-the-art baselines. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline oversampling methods in the comparative experiments.
evidence: In the results table, CTGAN [20] is listed alongside SMOTE, ADASYN, B-SMOTE and other methods as one of the comparative baselines used in the experiments.
venue: ICASSP 2025

title: AI-Ready Multimodal Data Pipeline to Enrich Cancer Care
summary: This paper presents an AI-ready multimodal data integration pipeline that combines structured EHR data, clinical notes, and imaging data to predict radiation therapy interruptions in cancer patients. Due to small sample size and patient privacy concerns, the authors generate a 5,000-record synthetic dataset used for training and validating their RTI prediction model. CTGAN is run directly to learn the joint distribution of the structured dataset and produce the synthetic patient records that form the training data for the case study.

title: SyntAR: Synthetic data generation using multiscale attention generator-discriminator framework (SinGAN-MSA) for improved aircraft recognition in remote sensing images
summary: This paper proposes SinGAN-MSA, a single-image adversarial generator-discriminator framework with multi-scale attention, to synthesize satellite images containing aircraft for improving aircraft detection and classification under data scarcity. The authors evaluate their synthetic 'SyntAR' images against real, synthetic, and hybrid training mixes and benchmark against YOLOv8 as a discriminator. In their related-work survey of synthetic data generation techniques, they list Synthetic Data Vault with Gaussian Copula (SDV-G) and Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (SDV-GAN) alongside GANs, VAEs, SMOTE and other methods, citing the original SDV paper without running it in their own experiments.
evidence: "Synthetic Data Vault with Gaussian Copula (SDV-G) [27], Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (SDV-GAN)" is listed among prior synthetic data generation techniques in the related-work discussion, not run in the authors' own experiments.
venue: Multimedia Tools and Applications

title: SynthEquity: A Privacy-Preserving Computational Framework for Identifying and Mitigating Medical Deserts Using Generative AI
summary: SynthEquity is a privacy-preserving framework that models healthcare access disparities by generating synthetic populations from public demographic and spatial data, combining them with an interpretable regression risk model and a browser-resident dashboard for real-time scenario analysis, demonstrated in a San Francisco case study and multi-city simulations. The framework's generative stage trains a Conditional Tabular GAN 'implemented through the Synthetic Data Vault ecosystem' to produce the synthetic populations that feed all downstream risk analysis, making SDV's CTGAN the load-bearing generator of the entire pipeline.
evidence: "The generative stage uses a Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network implemented through the Synthetic Data Vault ecosystem [2]."
venue: AIiH 2026 (Springer LNCS)

title: Synthesis of Hybrid Data Consisting of Chest Radiographs and Tabular Clinical Records Using Dual Generative Models for COVID-19 Positive Cases
summary: This paper proposes a method to generate synthetic hybrid medical data combining chest X-ray images and tabular clinical records for COVID-19 patients, by encoding CXRs with a pretrained auto-encoding GAN (αGAN), merging the encoded features with tabular clinical variables, and training a tabular generative model on the combined representation before decoding synthetic images back out. The resulting synthetic dataset was evaluated by comparing patient-outcome prediction performance when trained on real, synthetic, or combined data. CTGAN, obtained as the stand-alone sdv-dev/CTGAN library, is run directly as the generative network for the merged tabular-plus-encoded-image records, making it the core engine of the paper's synthesis pipeline.

University of Tokyo Hospital; Chiba University
evidence: "We used the stand-alone library, CTGAN (version 0.7.4; https://github.com/sdv-dev/CTGAN)" trained on merged encoded-image and tabular clinical data to produce the entire synthetic hybrid dataset evaluated in the study.

title: Data Synthesis Reinvented: Preserving Missing Patterns for Enhanced Analysis
summary: The paper proposes HottGen, a framework that augments existing synthetic-data generators (GAN, VAE, Bayesian Network based) so that they preserve both the observable and the missing-data distributions of real data, rather than discarding missingness during preprocessing. The authors instantiate HottGAN, HottVAE, and HottBN variants and evaluate them across multiple missingness mechanisms (MCAR/MAR/MNAR) on diverse datasets, showing improved fidelity over deletion, imputation, and complete-case baselines. CTGAN is run directly from its Python package with default configuration as the GAN backbone for the HottGAN variant, serving as one of the three generative models the empirical study is built on.
evidence: "All our methods are implemented using Python 3.6.0, PyTorch 1.8.0, and CTGAN [30] (which is the state-of-the-art tabular data generation model and can handle mixed data types) with its default configuration."
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
needs: Metadata lists only tgan-2018 as the cited SDV paper, but the body text explicitly names and runs CTGAN[30]/[32] as a distinct backbone generator; treated here per the body's actual usage.

title: Data Synthesis for Testing Black-Box Machine Learning Models
summary: This paper presents AITEST, a framework for automated synthesis of test data to evaluate black-box ML/DL classification models on tabular data, using constraint-based generation combined with a model-agnostic path coverage criterion derived from a global explainability algorithm (TREPAN) to test properties like fairness and robustness. The metadata indicates the paper cites the CTGAN paper, but no passage naming CTGAN, SDV, or any related component appears anywhere in the retrieved full text, so the citation could not be located or verified in context.

title: Synthesize, Adapt, Steal: A Few-Shot Domain Adaptive Model Stealing Attack for Tabular Data
summary: This paper proposes a few-shot, domain-adaptive model-stealing attack against black-box tabular ML models, combining synthetic query generation, a hybrid active-learning/adversarial query strategy, and a novel Relational Attention Corrector that enforces semantic validity. It is evaluated on an energy-sector intrusion-detection dataset (ERENO) and on Adult Income and Diabetes benchmarks, outperforming prior attacks and generator baselines like TabDDPM and GReaT. CTGAN is run as the core generator producing the synthetic data pool used to craft attack queries, and is benchmarked against diffusion- and LLM-based alternatives.

title: Synthesized Blood Test Data for Dementia Risk Screening Using Generative Adversarial Networks
summary: This conference paper investigates using CTGAN-based data augmentation to improve dementia risk prediction from basic blood test data, training linear regression and random forest models on real plus synthesized patient records from 202 inpatients and evaluating on 137 external participants. The authors explicitly identify their tool as 'the CTGAN open-source library in the Synthetic Data Vault project' and use Column Shape and Column Pair Trends scores to assess synthetic data quality. SDV's CTGAN is run directly as the generator producing the augmented training data, and its SDMetrics-style quality scores underpin the paper's central empirical claims.
evidence: "The CTGAN open-source library in the Synthetic Data Vault project is adept at capturing complex relationships between variables in a table format... Column Shape (CS) and Column Pair Trends (CPT) scores were compared to evaluate their similarity to the original training data."

title: Synthesizing Accurate Relational Data under Differential Privacy
summary: This paper introduces MARE, a differentially private relational data synthesis algorithm designed to preserve inter-table and inter-row correlations (parent-child, sequential, associative) in structurally complex data such as electronic health records, where existing methods either ignore correlations or suffer a dimensionality explosion. The authors validate MARE on MIMIC-IV-derived and private hospital datasets, showing it retains semantically valid patient trajectories with strong privacy guarantees. In their related-work discussion they describe SDV's HMA1 algorithm as a copula-based hierarchical synthesizer that, like PrivLava, fails to model intra-table (sequential) correlations, positioning it as prior art their method improves on rather than a baseline they run.
evidence: "HMA1, proposed under the system SDV [13], is a generalized approach for generating hierarchical synthetic data... it does not model intra-table correlations."
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (Big Data)

title: Synthesizing Feature-Aligned and Category-Aware Electronic Medical Records for Intracranial Aneurysm Rupture Prediction
summary: This paper introduces TransCGAN, a Transformer-based conditional GAN that generates category-balanced synthetic electronic medical records to improve intracranial aneurysm rupture prediction under data scarcity and class imbalance. The authors' conditional resampling module draws inspiration from CTGAN's conditional generation mechanism, and they separately re-implemented CTGAN (and Table-GAN) using released code as comparison baselines against their own model. CTGAN's conditional sampling design is thus both an architectural influence and a benchmarked baseline generator in the empirical evaluation.

title: On Synthesizing Network Traces – Case Studies in Network Steganalysis and Packet Analysis
summary: This conference paper discusses the general use of synthetic data and presents a methodology for synthesizing network traces (PCAP files) for two case studies: an entropy-based network steganalysis technique and a network packet analysis teaching exercise. It surveys related synthetic-data work across domains such as software testing and learning analytics before detailing its own trace-synthesis approach. SDV's original DSAA paper is cited only as a bibliographic example of preserving statistical properties in generated synthetic data, with no SDV code run.

title: Synthesizing Privacy Preserving Entity Resolution Datasets
summary: This paper proposes a differentially private framework for synthesizing surrogate entity resolution (ER) datasets by learning the similarity distributions of matching and non-matching entity pairs from a real dataset and sampling fake entities and pairs that preserve those distributions while protecting privacy. It targets the goal that ER matchers trained on the synthetic data perform close to those trained on the real data, and evaluates this on several ER benchmarks. It cites CTGAN among prior GAN-based approaches to relational data synthesis, noting these works can only synthesize a single table, positioning its own transformer-based, multi-artifact approach against them without running CTGAN itself.
evidence: "GAN based works [15], [16], [17], [18] can only synthesize one table." -- CTGAN (ctgan-neurips-2019) is cited among prior GAN-based relational data synthesis methods that the paper explicitly contrasts itself against, but it is not run or benchmarked.

title: Synthesizing Quality Open Data Assets from Private Health Research Studies
summary: The authors present HealthGAN, a Wasserstein-GAN-based synthetic data generation method used to reproduce two prior autism spectrum disorder studies from a private health data warehouse while preserving patient privacy. They extend HealthGAN with a novel categorical/ordinal encoding scheme and evaluate the resulting synthetic data for privacy, resemblance, utility, and efficiency. The encoding scheme is described as a 'novel variant' of the categorical encoding method from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), which SDV's reversible transform technique is adapted and extended rather than run directly.
evidence: "This method is based on the Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network [2,5] and uses a novel variant of the categorical encoding method from 'The Synthetic data vault' (SDV) [9]."
venue: BIS 2020 Workshops (LNBIP 394)

title: Synthesizing Realistic Data with GANs: Balancing Quality, Similarity, and Privacy
summary: This is a comparative survey and small experimental study of GAN-based tabular synthetic-data generators (MedGAN, TableGAN, CTGAN, CW-GAN, PATE-GAN, SDV, FakeDB), evaluating a subset of them on machine-learning utility, statistical similarity, and privacy leakage metrics on a shared dataset. SDV is discussed in its own section, described as using Bayesian networks to model dependencies between tables and columns, but it is not included among the four generators actually run in the experiments (MedGAN, CTGAN, TableGAN, CW-GAN). CTGAN is treated as one of several evaluation subjects, with its architecture, training-by-sampling method and mode-specific normalization described at length before being scored in the results tables, while SDV itself is only cited and described, never executed.
evidence: "In this section, we focus on evaluating four GAN-based tabular data generators: MedGAN, CTGAN, TableGAN, and CW-GAN" — SDV is discussed separately via Bayesian-network formulas but excluded from the run experiments, while CTGAN appears in Tables 3-5 results.

title: Synthetic Augmentation of Structured Templates for Geo-Localization
summary: This paper proposes a data-centric framework for visual geo-localization that encodes images into interpretable 'Structured Templates' capturing environmental, infrastructural, and cultural attributes via a vision-language model, then augments underrepresented countries in a long-tail YFCC100M subset using tabular oversampling methods. It compares SMOTENC, ADASYN, KMeans-SMOTE, and CTGAN as synthetic sampling techniques applied to the encoded template feature vectors, finding SMOTENC best overall but CTGAN competitive for countries with complex geographic patterns. CTGAN is run as one of several oversampling baselines on structured tabular feature representations, not as the paper's proposed method.
evidence: "We compare four oversampling methods—ADASYN, CTGAN, SMOTENC, and KMeans-SMOTE—against a baseline model trained only on real data," with CTGAN achieving F1 0.300 vs SMOTENC's 0.376 in Table 3.

title: Synthetic Benchmarks for Genetic Improvement
summary: This short paper proposes a method for constructing synthetic benchmarks for genetic improvement (GI), aiming to circumvent the high cost of evaluating real-world software by generating artificial scenarios with statistics drawn from real cases. The work is a position/method paper describing the approach at a high level, without implementing or running any specific data-synthesis tool. SDV is cited only in a passing background sentence noting that artificial data generation is common in machine learning and data science, with no engagement with its methods.
evidence: "Generating artificial data is often done when data is too scarce or too expensive to obtain [4], and mostly prevalent in machine learning and data science [5]." where [5] is the SDV DSAA 2016 paper, cited only in the reference list and this background sentence.
venue: IEEE/ACM 42nd International Conference on Software Engineering Workshops (ICSEW'20)

title: Synthetic Blood Data Generation for Fair Machine Learning
summary: This paper benchmarks seven generative models—CTGAN, TVAE, Gaussian Copula, CopulaGAN, MedGAN, DiscGAN, and FAST-ML—for synthesizing clinical blood test and demographic data across three medical datasets (an Irish hospital dataset, a UCI dataset, and the Korean NHIS 2002 dataset), evaluating them on statistical fidelity (KS, Wasserstein distance, JSD) and demographic fairness. It finds Gaussian Copula, TVAE, and CTGAN consistently achieve the best fidelity and least bias amplification, while MedGAN and DiscGAN degrade subgroup representation. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, Gaussian Copula and CopulaGAN synthesizers are run directly as four of the seven evaluated generative models and emerge as the top performers across all three datasets.
evidence: "Seven generative models—CTGAN, TVAE, Gaussian Copula, CopulaGAN, MedGAN, DiscGAN, and FASTML—are applied to generate synthetic records." Results show Gaussian Copula, TVAE, and CTGAN as the best-performing model on each of the three datasets respectively.

It surveys practical open-source libraries and frameworks rather than running any experiments of its own. The Synthetic Data Vault is cited and briefly described as providing modular tools for tabular, relational, and time-series synthesis, alongside CTGAN/TGAN and YData-Synthetic, purely as prior art discussed in the related-work/library-overview section.

title: Synthetic Data Approach for Classification and Regression
summary: This paper proposes a Synthetic Data Approach for Classification and Regression (SDAC/SDAR), which uses probability distribution estimation combined with a k-nearest neighbor model to generate synthetic data for machine learning tasks facing insufficient or privacy-restricted samples. It positions its method against prior approaches including SMOTE and GAN, evaluating on five public datasets for classification and regression. SDV (the Synthetic Data Vault) is cited and described in related work as a relational-database synthesizing approach the authors contrast their method against, but it is not run in the experiments.

title: Synthetic Climate Data Generation Using Generative Adversarial Networks for Drought Modelling in Southern Africa
summary: This conference paper applies generative adversarial networks to reconstruct missing long-term soil moisture and sunshine duration time series for drought modelling in data-scarce Southern Africa, producing a 50-year hybrid dataset used as input to random forest and feedforward neural network drought prediction models. The authors' own GAN is a custom time-series model, not the SDV package, but they cite CTGAN's reported AUC results as a comparable benchmark discussed in prose. title: Synthetic Collision-Prone Trajectory Data Generation Using CTGAN for Connected Autonomous Vehicles
summary: This conference paper proposes a pipeline for generating synthetic collision-prone vehicle trajectories to support testing and validation of connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs), addressing the scarcity and privacy limitations of real-world crash data. The authors configure, condition, and train a CTGAN model on labeled real-world trajectory data (from ApolloScape and nuScenes) to produce diverse collision scenarios, comparing its output against TimeGAN and SocialGAN on realism, diversity, and coverage metrics. CTGAN is the sole generative model driving the entire empirical study, run to condition synthetic trajectory generation on collision-relevant labels.

title: Using synthetic data to develop machine learning models to predict the performance of fiber-reinforced concrete
summary: This study compiles a fiber-reinforced concrete dataset from 18 published papers and augments it with synthetic data to train multiple linear regression, SVR, random forest, and gradient boosting models predicting concrete toughness. The authors used the Synthetic Data Vault package (v1.2.0) to generate synthetic toughness-factor data within defined value ranges, and used SDMetrics (v0.10.1) to compute quality scores and column-pair trend analyses validating the synthetic data against the original distribution. SDV's synthesizer and SDMetrics' quality-report evaluation are run directly as the load-bearing data-augmentation pipeline underlying the whole modeling effort.

The authors report better testing accuracy with larger synthetic datasets and build toward a personalized treatment-plan GUI. They cite SDV's CTGANSynthesizer documentation directly for the model's hyperparameters (epochs, batch size, learning rate, pac), indicating the SDV package's CTGAN implementation is the generator producing all synthetic training data.

title: Synthetic Data-Driven Learning for IoMT Applications
summary: This single-author conference paper investigates whether CTGAN-generated synthetic IoMT (Internet of Medical Things) sensor data can substitute for real patient data when training machine learning classifiers, and whether CTGAN can be used to augment imbalanced medical datasets. Four ML models (XGBoost, SVM, logistic regression, ANN) are trained and compared on real versus CTGAN-synthesized data, finding no significant performance difference for synthesis but degraded performance when CTGAN is used for class-imbalance augmentation. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN with its mode-specific normalization and conditional vector, is run directly as the sole synthetic data generator underpinning the entire empirical study.
evidence: "The experimental results show that there is no difference in classification reports... in using the synthetic IoMT dataset generated by CTGAN to train four different ML models compared to using the original dataset." CTGAN is also used to augment the imbalanced dataset.

title: Tabular GAN-Based Oversampling of Imbalanced Time-to-Event Data for Survival Prediction

It finds that traditional resampling methods generally outperform GAN-based ones on both synthetic sample fidelity and downstream survival prediction accuracy. CTGAN is one of the four GAN baselines run and evaluated as a minority-class oversampler, described as using mode-specific normalization and conditional-generator/training-by-sampling techniques.
evidence: "Four tabular GAN-based methods (CTGAN, CTAB-GAN, CTAB-GAN+ and FCT-GAN) and three traditional methods (SMOTE, SVMSMOTE and BorderlineSMOTE) are used to generate synthetic data of minority classes in four datasets"
venue: 2023 8th International Conference on Cloud Computing and Big Data Analytics (ICCCBDA)
needs: Not explicitly stated whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or a reimplementation was used; treated as api_user given no reimplementation details are given.

title: Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks with an Enhanced Sampling Approach for High-Quality Cardiovascular Disease Dataset Generation
summary: This conference paper proposes an enhanced sampling approach for GAN-based generation of synthetic cardiovascular disease tabular data, aiming to improve resemblance to real clinical/demographic/laboratory data distributions under conditions of missing values and class imbalance. The authors evaluate their model against CTGAN using Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics, Jaccard coefficients, and CDF comparisons across continuous and categorical CVD variables. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN with mode-specific normalization and a conditional generator, is run as the sole comparison baseline throughout the empirical evaluation.
evidence: "the performance of the proposed method was evaluated by comparing it with the data generated from the CTGAN" -- CTGAN is the sole benchmark across KS-statistic, Jaccard coefficient, and CDF comparisons throughout the results section.
venue: TrustCom 2023

title: Tabular Learning-Based Traffic Event Prediction for Intelligent Social Transportation System
summary: This paper proposes a tabular learning framework using the TabNet model to predict traffic events by integrating social traffic data, with model interpretability analysis to assess the importance of external traffic factors for autonomous driving and traffic planning applications. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing within a related-work discussion of prior deep neural network architectures for tabular data, alongside TabNN, without being run or evaluated. SDV's CTGAN is cited only as one of several prior tabular DNN architectures that did not achieve overwhelming performance.

title: Tabular Synthesis Based on Bi-Directional Feedback Conditional Diffusion Models
summary: This ICASSP paper proposes BiFeD, a bi-directional feedback conditional diffusion model that models continuous and discrete tabular variables with separate, mutually conditioning diffusion processes, augmented with contrastive and multi-task learning, and shows state-of-the-art results across 15 tabular datasets against diffusion- and GAN-based baselines (TableGAN, RelDDPM, OCT-GAN, RNODE, STaSy, Codi). CTGAN is not among the run baselines; it is cited in the introduction as prior art whose variational Gaussian mixture normalization technique motivates the paper's discussion of continuous-variable preprocessing. SDV's CTGAN and its mode-specific (variational Gaussian mixture) normalization are referenced only in prose to motivate the approach, not executed or benchmarked.
evidence: "continuous variables benefit from normalization techniques such as variational Gaussian mixture models [9]" -- ref [9] is Xu & Veeramachaneni's CTGAN paper, cited only in the introduction; CTGAN is absent from the actual experimental baselines (TableGAN, RelDDPM, OCT-GAN, RNODE, STaSy, Codi).
venue: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing

title: Tabular Data Synthesis with GANs for Adaptive AI Models
summary: This paper presents CustomGAN, a framework for generating synthetic tabular data that satisfies user-specified marginal-distribution constraints while preserving the correlations of the original data, aimed at producing customized test/training data for adaptive AI models under distribution shift. The architecture trains a CTGAN model on the original dataset and then a second CTGAN on sampler-transformed data, using CTGAN's conditional generation to iteratively steer output columns toward target marginal distributions. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator are the core mechanisms the whole pipeline is built around, run as the actual synthetic-data generator, while SDV's original Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in passing as an example of copula-based statistical modeling approaches.
evidence: "Firstly, a CTGAN model is trained using the original dataset... Since CTGAN is a conditional GAN, generating rows that have a specific discrete column value is straightforward." The whole CustomGAN pipeline trains and re-trains CTGAN as its generator.
venue: 7th Joint International Conference on Data Science & Management of Data (11th ACM IKDD CODS and 29th COMAD) (CODS-COMAD 2024)

title: Tabular data synthesis with generative adversarial networks: design space and optimizations
summary: This VLDB Journal article presents a unified GAN-based framework for tabular data synthesis, defining a design space of neural architectures, training strategies, and normalization techniques, and reporting extensive experiments comparing GAN-based methods against conventional privacy-preserving data publishing approaches. The authors adopt CTGAN's GMM-based mode-specific normalization and its conditional-vector mechanism as design choices within their own framework rather than running the SDV library itself, while the original Synthetic Data Vault paper appears only in the reference list with no further discussion in the body text. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional sampling design are described and reimplemented in the authors' own prose as one design option among many, and SDV (Patki et al. 2016) is cited only bibliographically.

title: TabularFM: An Open Framework For Tabular Foundational Models
summary: This paper introduces TabularFM, an open-source framework for pretraining and benchmarking tabular foundational models across a thousand curated tabular datasets (GitTables and Kaggle), covering GAN-, VAE-, and Transformer-based architectures. Its core empirical programme pretrains CTGAN and TVAE, and introduces new variants (STVAE, STVAEM) that modify TVAE's architecture to improve cross-dataset transferability, evaluating outputs with column-shape and column-pair-trend similarity scores resembling SDMetrics' quality report. CTGAN and TVAE, the neural synthesizers from the SDV/CTGAN family, are pretrained, benchmarked, and structurally extended (via STVAE/STVAEM) as the paper's central generative models.

title: A Tale of Two Methods: Unveiling the Limitations of GAN and the Rise of Bayesian Networks for Synthetic Network Traffic Generation
summary: This paper proposes a comprehensive set of quality metrics (covering realism, diversity, novelty, and protocol compliance) for evaluating synthetic legitimate network traffic, and uses them to empirically compare several network-flow generation methods including GAN-based approaches and Bayesian Networks. Across two feature sets and a third dataset, the authors find that Bayesian Networks generally outperform GAN-based generators on their proposed metrics while being far cheaper computationally. CTGAN is run as one of seven benchmarked traffic generators, its training time, correlation-capture, and mode-invention behavior analyzed in detail alongside E-WGAN-GP and NetShare.

title: A Novel Technique of Synthetic Data Generation for Asset Administration Shells in Industry 4.0 Scenarios
summary: This paper proposes AASGAN, a method that combines the Asset Administration Shell (AAS) knowledge representation used for Industry 4.0 digital twins with a GAN-based synthetic data generator, aiming to let manufacturers share realistic but non-confidential equipment and spare-parts data across an OEM network. The authors convert AAS submodels into tabular form and train a generative model to produce fake records that mimic the real data's statistical properties, later validated with the table_evaluator package. The Python 'ctgan' library is used directly as the generator, fitting and sampling synthetic tabular records from the AAS-derived tables, making CTGAN the core synthesis engine of the whole empirical pipeline.

summary: This paper proposes TempEHR, a framework for synthesizing electronic health records that models temporal irregularities using a time-aware Maximum Mean Discrepancy VAE with T-LSTM layers and a novel TrendFinder module for capturing temporal trends, evaluated on MIMIC-IV data for utility, fidelity, and privacy. title: Temporal Causal Discovery with Counterfactual Data Augmentation for Automotive Fault Diagnosis
summary: This paper proposes TCDI, a temporal causal discovery method for automotive sensor data combining lag detection, temporal conditional independence testing, and effect-type analysis, plus CDA, a counterfactual data augmentation method that generates synthetic fault samples respecting discovered causal structure and physical constraints. Experiments on real automotive data show TCDI outperforms baseline causal discovery methods and CDA produces physically valid samples where other augmentation methods fail. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of deep generative models that can violate physical laws, with no library run.

The authors survey existing tools (Fairness Indicators, Aequitas, Alibi) that could support such testing. title: Testing Object Detection for Autonomous Driving Systems via 3D Reconstruction
summary: This paper proposes an automatic method for testing DNN-based object detection in autonomous driving systems by synthesizing natural-looking images via 3D reconstruction of vehicles inserted into real driving photos, evaluated on 500 Apollo dataset photos. The approach uses vanishing point estimation and heuristic-based image insertion rather than any generative model. The original SDV paper is cited once in passing to support the general claim that artificial data can partially replace real data, with no SDV component or method actually used.

summary: This paper proposes a text data annotation model that fuses domain knowledge graphs with Bayesian inference networks, using the knowledge graph to extract semantic classes and concept relationships and plain Bayesian mapping inference to resolve ambiguity in fuzzy concepts. It targets the problem of obtaining high-quality labels for unstructured text data where predefined data models are lacking. title: Theseus Data Synthesis Approach: A Privacy-Preserving Online Data Sharing Service
summary: This paper proposes the Theseus Data Synthesis Approach (TDSA), a privacy-preserving synthetic data generation method that iteratively replaces partial records until no original record remains, aiming to balance cloud data sharing utility with personal privacy. It compares TDSA conceptually against other anonymization and synthesis techniques such as k-anonymity, differential privacy, and prior synthesizers, evaluating quality and utility of the resulting synthetic dataset. SDV (the Synthetic Data Vault) is mentioned only in related-work discussion describing its use of column probability distributions and covariances, without being run or benchmarked in the experiments.

title: A Three-Way Knot: Privacy, Fairness, and Predictive Performance Dynamics
summary: This paper investigates the three-way trade-offs between privacy, fairness, and predictive performance in machine learning models trained on synthetic data. The authors generate multiple privacy-protected variants of benchmark FAccT datasets and evaluate how optimizing one dimension affects the other two, finding that joint gains in fairness and performance come at the cost of privacy. The synthetic data variants are produced by running the SDV package's CopulaGAN, TVAE, and CTGAN synthesizers with varied hyperparameters (epochs, batch size, embedding dimension) and conditional sampling to protect single-out instances.

summary: This paper studies the use of TimeGAN to generate synthetic time-series telemetry and video-QoS data for a Programmable Data Plane scenario, using that synthetic data to train a Reinforcement Learning agent that optimizes switch buffer sizes, and reporting 99% QoS similarity to real-setup training. title: A Timing Prediction Framework for Wide Voltage Design with Data Augmentation Strategy
summary: This ASPDAC 2021 paper proposes a LightGBM-based framework to predict circuit path delays across wide-voltage PVT corners, addressing the scarcity of low-voltage timing data by augmenting training sets with synthetic samples. The authors reimplement CTGAN's conditional generator and discriminator architecture themselves, explicitly replacing the original ReLU activation with GeLU, and combine its output with SMOTER-generated samples to train the delay predictor. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator design are reproduced and modified in the authors' own implementation to generate the synthetic circuit-delay data underlying the whole empirical evaluation.

title: Tool/Dataset Paper: Realistic ABAC Data Generation using Conditional Tabular GAN
summary: This paper introduces ConGRASS, a web-based tool that trains a conditional tabular GAN on a real Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) dataset to generate arbitrarily large, realistic synthetic ABAC datasets for reproducible access-control research. The authors explicitly use the CTGAN library from the SDV ecosystem as their generative model, and evaluate outputs using the SDV/SDMetrics CSTest score and the Table Evaluator tool associated with SDV. CTGAN, run as the core generator of the entire pipeline, is the load-bearing component of the whole empirical study.
