title: Topology for Preserving Feature Correlation in Tabular Synthetic Data
summary: This short theoretical paper investigates whether preserving the topological structure of synthetic tabular data—via persistent homology and homeomorphism between original and synthetic data spaces—can preserve pairwise feature correlations, which GAN-based synthesizers otherwise fail to retain. The authors import a CTGAN model from its GitHub repository, generate synthetic data for datasets including a wine-quality dataset, and empirically show that CT-GAN's output has dissimilar 0th and 1st homology groups from the real data, evidencing broken feature correlations. CTGAN (with its mode-specific normalization) is the sole generative model run in the study, serving as the empirical subject whose correlation-preservation failure motivates the paper's topological hypothesis.
evidence: "First, we imported the CT-GAN model from the Github repository and generated synthetic data for each of the dataset... It is evident from this figure that the pairwise correlations among the features are not preserved in the synthetic data generated by the CT-GAN model."
venue: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES) / SIN 2022

title: TOR-GANXAI: Assessing the Validity of Synthetic Torrefaction Data for ML Applications in Bioenergy
summary: This paper investigates whether CTGAN-generated synthetic tabular data can substitute for scarce real experimental data in training ML models (XGBoost) for lignocellulosic biomass torrefaction, using an extensive suite of statistical similarity tests (KS test, KL divergence, Wasserstein distance, MMD, etc.) and downstream predictive performance to judge fidelity. It finds that while operational parameters are well replicated, key outputs like yield and HHV are poorly captured, so models trained on synthetic data generalize badly to real cases. The CTGAN synthesizer was implemented using the CTGANSynthesizer module from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, run as the sole synthetic-data generator underlying the entire empirical evaluation.

title: TRACE: Transformer-Based Risk Assessment for Clinical Evaluation

title: TRamCol-Diff: Deepening Diffusion Model Comprehension for Extensive Categorical Medical Service Data
summary: This paper proposes TRamCol-Diff, a diffusion-model-based tabular data generator for Medical Service Data that uses a random column rearrangement (TRamCol) strategy to help the model learn implicit inter-column relationships and improve synthetic data fidelity. It benchmarks TRamCol-Diff against NFlow, ADS-GAN, PATE-GAN, TVAE, CTGAN, and TabDDPM, reporting quantitative fidelity/utility metrics for each, and also tests TRamCol combined with each baseline. title: Trans-CTGAN: A Transformer-Enhanced GAN Model for Correlation-Preserving Tabular Data Generation
summary: This paper proposes Trans-CTGAN, a modified version of CTGAN that inserts multi-head Transformer attention into both the generator and discriminator to better model inter-feature correlations, while removing CTGAN's PacGAN component, and evaluates it on five public tabular datasets against CTABGAN, CTGAN, TVAE and TabDDPM using correlation-matrix distance and ML utility metrics. The paper fundamentally redesigns CTGAN's architecture, including its conditional vector design, mode-specific normalization, and training sampling scheme, into a new Transformer-augmented generator, and separately runs CTGAN and TVAE (via the Synthcity framework) as comparison baselines throughout the experiments.

title: A transfer learning based CNN for dynamic security assessment with small datasets and unknown data
summary: This paper proposes a dynamic security assessment (DSA) model for power systems that combines CTGAN-based data augmentation with a CNN classifier and transfer-learning fine-tuning to handle small datasets and unknown fault/topology conditions, tested on the IEEE 39-bus system. title: TreeCSP: An Efficient Way to Generate Household Relationships for Population Synthesis
summary: This paper introduces TreeCSP, a Tree-based Chained Sampling Pools framework for population synthesis in agent-based transport models, which organizes household and person generation via a hierarchical relationship tree and multi-step sampling to better capture complex household structures than existing methods. title: TrustGenTable: A Trusted Method for Generating Tabular Data
summary: This paper proposes TrustGenTable, an architecture for generating trustworthy tabular data that pairs a novel distribution-capturing generator with a checking mechanism (specific and adaptive checks, including denial constraints) to flag untrustworthy synthetic records, aiming to mitigate data scarcity in fields like healthcare. It is evaluated on four real-world datasets against several generative baselines including CLBN, MedGAN, VeeGAN, TableGAN, TVAE and CTGAN, with TVAE singled out as the strongest baseline for correlation and clustering comparisons. title: TSDCG: Tabular Synthetic Data with Code Generation LLMs
summary: This paper proposes TSDCG, a method that uses code-generating LLMs combined with data profiling to synthesize tabular data faster and more cheaply than model-training-based approaches. It benchmarks TSDCG against GReaT, TVAE, and CTGAN on the iris dataset, reporting per-iteration training time and distributional similarity metrics, and claims comparable or better quality at lower cost. CTGAN and TVAE are run as baseline generators against which the authors' LLM-based TSDCG is compared.

title: A Study on TVAE-Based Data Augmentation and Verification to Predict Physiologically Active Ingredients of Medicine Plants According to Climate Change
summary: This conference paper proposes a pipeline to predict physiologically active ingredient levels (phenol, flavonoid) in Cnidium Officinale, a climate-vulnerable medicinal plant, under different SSP climate scenarios. To overcome limited and imbalanced experimental data, the authors augment their collected environmental/physiological dataset with the TVAE algorithm, assess the synthetic data's fidelity using column shape and column pair trends metrics (89% overall quality), then train RF, SVR, XGBoost, AdaBoost and LightGBM models on the augmented data, finding XGBoost most accurate. TVAE, from the CTGAN package, is run directly as the data-augmentation generator underpinning the entire downstream prediction pipeline, with its output quality scored via SDMetrics-style column-level metrics.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Traffic Forecasting Using Deep-Ensemble-Based Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks
summary: This paper proposes a scalable deep-ensemble approach for quantifying data and model uncertainty in spatiotemporal graph neural networks used for traffic forecasting, combining simultaneous quantile regression loss, scalable Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, and Gaussian copula-based generative modeling to construct diverse high-performing model ensembles. The approach is demonstrated on a diffusion convolutional recurrent neural network for short-term traffic forecasting and shown to outperform existing Bayesian and frequentist uncertainty estimation baselines. The SDV package (v0.14.0) is used directly to fit the multivariate Gaussian Copula models that generate new high-performing hyperparameter configurations for the ensemble.

title: UniFi-LLM: A Unified Large Language Model for Financial Data Generation and Fraud Prediction
summary: This paper proposes UniFi-LLM, a unified large language model that uses schema-aware prompt templates, column-conditioned LoRA adapters, and structured output enforcement to jointly perform synthetic financial data generation and fraud prediction. It reports experiments on open-source credit card datasets showing UniFi-LLM outperforms GAN, VAE, and diffusion-based generators in fidelity and fraud-classification metrics. CTGAN is cited only in passing as a specialized prior model that LLM-based approaches must match through fine-tuning, with no experiments run using it.

In its GAN section the survey describes tabular-data synthesis methods including TableGAN, and characterizes CTGAN's architecture and its likelihood-fitness/ML-efficacy evaluation framework, noting TVAE as a variational-autoencoder alternative introduced in the same work. Neither model is run by the authors; CTGAN and TVAE are only described as prior work from the cited paper.

title: Utility of GAN generated synthetic data for cardiovascular diseases mortality prediction: an experimental study
summary: This paper reports a controlled experimental study evaluating the utility of GAN-generated synthetic electronic health records for predicting cardiovascular disease mortality, comparing CTGAN, LSTM-GAN and DP-GAN across multiple datasets and classifiers using TSTR/TRTS evaluation protocols. A second experiment isolates CTGAN alone to study how increasing feature dimensionality affects synthetic data utility. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run directly as one of the generative models compared and is reported as the best-performing model overall.

title: Utility Meets Privacy: A Critical Evaluation of Tabular Data Synthesizers
summary: This paper benchmarks 12 tabular data synthesizers across 17 health datasets, introducing a utility-privacy score that combines machine-learning utility with an extended membership-inference privacy measure to quantify their trade-off. It finds that no single synthesizer dominates across datasets, that utility and privacy improvements trade off against each other, and that robustness to data properties varies by method. Among the 12 synthesizers evaluated, SDV's Gaussian Copula Synthesizer, CTGAN, and TVAE are run as evaluation subjects alongside SMOTE, PrivBayes, CART, GReaT and others.

title: Utility and Privacy Assessment of Synthetic Microbiome Data
summary: This paper empirically evaluates two open-source synthetic data generation tools, the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) and synthpop, on several publicly available human microbiome datasets, assessing both machine-learning utility and privacy risk (via nearest-neighbor distance to original samples). The authors find both tools yield synthetic data with ML performance close to the original, but SDV's synthetic samples show larger minimal distances to real records, suggesting lower re-identification risk than synthpop. SDV's GaussianCopula model is run directly (via the reticulate Python interface) as one of the two synthesizers whose output forms the entire empirical comparison.

title: Utility and Privacy Assessments of Synthetic Data for Regression Tasks
summary: This paper evaluates several synthetic data generation methods -- the Synthetic Data Vault, DataSynthesizer, and synthpop -- for their utility in regression tasks and studies the risk of attribute disclosure on the resulting synthetic datasets. The authors run SDV's Gaussian copula synthesizer to generate synthetic data from real datasets, treating it as one of three synthesizers compared for regression utility and privacy risk, extending prior categorical attribute-disclosure measures to numeric attributes. SDV's Gaussian copula model is run as one of the evaluation subjects generating synthetic data for the utility and privacy assessment.

title: On the Utility of Synthetic Data: An Empirical Evaluation on Machine Learning Tasks

The authors run SDV's default Gaussian Copula model to generate synthetic training data and compare downstream model performance and privacy-related distance metrics against DataSynthesizer with and without differential privacy. title: VAE-SMOTE Augmented Diffusion for Anomaly Detection
summary: This paper proposes VADAD, a diffusion-model-based unsupervised anomaly detection framework for tabular data that uses a truncated diffusion strategy for efficient inference and a novel VAE-enhanced SMOTE (VSA) data augmentation method to address limited training data. The authors compare their VSA augmentation strategy against TVAE- and CTGAN-based data augmentation on 18 real-world datasets, showing VSA outperforms both in AUC-ROC and AUC-PR. CTGAN and TVAE are run as comparison baselines for the data-augmentation ablation, benchmarked against the paper's own VAE-SMOTE approach.

title: VersaTable: Generating Realistic Mixed-Type Tables Blending Categorical Tags, Variable-Length Lists, and Free Text
summary: VersaTable is a two-stage LLM pipeline for synthesizing mixed-type tables that blend compact categorical/numeric attributes with variable-length lists and free-text banners, targeting cyber-defense host-configuration decoys as well as general tabular benchmarks. The authors motivate their design by contrasting it with prior GAN- and VAE-based tabular synthesizers, noting that CTGAN and TVAE are implemented in the SDV framework, which enforces a fixed set of column sdtypes (boolean, categorical, datetime, numerical, id) unable to represent long free text or nested lists. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE are discussed only as prior-art baselines whose metadata-schema constraints motivate VersaTable's approach, not run as experiments in the reported results.

title: Virtual Patient Model: An Approach for Generating Synthetic Healthcare Time Series Data
summary: This paper proposes the Virtual Patient Model (VPM), a system combining a genetic algorithm, statistical analysis, and machine learning to generate synthetic healthcare time-series data that preserves statistical similarity to real patient data while retaining differences useful for training predictive models. It validates VPM on real-world time-series datasets using statistical tests and comparative machine-learning classification performance. The paper cites the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper as prior work that synthesizes discrete relational data by sampling from a learned statistical distribution, contrasting it with VPM's time-series approach, but does not run SDV itself.

title: Virtual Wearable Sensor Data Generation with Generative Adversarial Networks
summary: This Winter Simulation Conference paper investigates DoppelGANger (DGAN), a time-series GAN, for generating subject-specific wearable sensor data derived from the NHANES health survey, evaluating its ability to preserve temporal and multi-dimensional statistical properties. The authors compare DGAN's synthetic attribute distributions against those produced by a second generator using KS-statistic tests across gender, age, and race attributes. CTGAN is run as a comparison benchmark to assess jointly-generated categorical attributes, with its conditional vector, generator loss, and training-by-sampling method described and its output measured against DGAN's.

title: A Visual Tool for Interactively Privacy Analysis and Preservation on Order-Dynamic Tabular Data
summary: This paper presents TPA (Tabular Privacy Assistant), an interactive visual tool for analyzing and mitigating privacy risks in tabular data whose attribute order is dynamically adjustable, using a data-cube backbone for real-time risk recalculation and offering several privacy-enhancement operations. One such operation, 'Adding Fake Data', uses CTGAN to train on selected records and generate synthetic records injected into the sheet to confuse attackers. CTGAN is thus run as one of several built-in privacy-enhancement techniques within the tool, not as the paper's central contribution.

title: Warts Disease Treatment Suggestion Using Images and Numerical Data
summary: This conference paper proposes a machine-learning and deep-learning framework that combines numerical and image data to classify wart treatment (cryotherapy vs. immunotherapy) for HPV-induced warts, achieving up to 91.67% accuracy on raw data. Because the original numerical dataset had only 90 points, the authors additionally used CTGAN alongside SMOTE to synthetically expand the dataset and tested classifiers on the combined data, though accuracy dropped when synthetic data was added. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run as a data-augmentation tool to increase dataset size, one of two synthetic-data-generation techniques compared in the study.

summary: This paper argues that AI-generated synthetic data (SD) can itself become adversarial background knowledge that undermines data anonymization, contrary to its usual framing as a privacy-protection tool. Using the Adult census dataset, the authors generate synthetic tabular data and use it to run six privacy-breach scenarios (attribute disclosure, group privacy disclosure, re-identification, etc.) against anonymized data. The CTGAN model is used throughout as the core generator, run with its conditional vector and mode normalization to produce the synthetic data that drives the entire empirical attack pipeline.
